final.memo:
Hertz Global Holdings is currently a classic example of a bankrupt entity where the equity is fundamentally worthless, yet the market has chosen to ignore the reality of its insolvency. The company filed for Chapter 11 on May 22, 2020, following a catastrophic drop in travel demand that rendered its $18.8bn debt load unsustainable [D03, D04].

Under the absolute priority rule of Chapter 11, senior claims including vehicle ABS and corporate debt must be fully satisfied before equity receives any consideration [D02, D05, D07]. With liabilities reaching $18.8bn, the recovery waterfall is effectively closed to shareholders [D04]. The current attempt to value the equity at nearly $800m is entirely detached from the recovery math, as there is no scenario in which asset realizations cover even the senior tranches [D04, D05].

The market's recent obsession with the common stock, including a 115.2% single-day rally on June 8, 2020, represents a speculative fervor divorced from the underlying bankruptcy process [D04]. This is not an event-driven opportunity for us; it is a liquidity trap. The bankruptcy court and senior creditors are now the sole decision-makers, and they have no incentive to preserve value for the equity holders who are structurally impaired [D03, D07].

Our mandate remains disciplined and value-focused. While others engage in sentiment-based trading, we recognize that when the math dictates an absolute loss, the only prudent decision is to step aside. We are passing on Hertz entirely, as there is no floor, no governance path, and no legitimate path to recovery for the common equity [D05, D07, D08].
